reaches.name: The origin: Satharai junction
reaches.verdict: Seasonal channel; fresh flow only by diversion when Poondi reservoir is full

channel.text: A new check dam across the Cooum at Perambakkam was sanctioned in February 2026: Rs 5.98 crore, 85 m long, 3.38 Mcft storage, 359.12 acres of ayacut, designed for a flood discharge of 10,556 cusecs at the site; the order places Kesavaram anicut 7.7 km upstream and the Puthumavilangai check dam 5 km downstream

surveys: No known public flow gauge on the river (IISc/IIT-M/IIT-B 2016; WRD CFM-DSS lists no Cooum station) - re-verify before any flow claim

facts.text: The Cooum originates at the junction of the Old Bangaru Channel with the surplus courses of the Cooum and Satharai tanks; WRD gives the river 65 km from here to the sea.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, sections 1.1.3 and 1.2

facts.text: Fresh water enters the river only when Poondi reservoir reaches its full level: 650 cusecs are diverted through Kesavaram anicut for 75 to 90 days, about 51.68 MCM in such a year.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, section 1.7

facts.text: Kesavaram anicut itself stands across the Kosasthalaiyar, not the Cooum; its regulated arm runs about 5 to 7.5 km before it becomes the Cooum - the same DPR calls it the Placis Canal (5 km) in one section and the Old Bangaru Channel (7.5 km) in another. Its construction date is not stated in any primary on our record.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum and Kosasthalaiyar Sub Basin DPRs

facts.text: OpenStreetMap maps no water surface on the first seven kilometres; outside the diversion season the channel here runs dry.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu OSM and Sentinel-2 analysis

facts.text: WRD's rain gauges record 712.78 mm a year at Kesavaram anicut and 1,207.97 mm at Korattur anicut.

In Villivakkam block, eleven tanks with 1,376.26 ha of registered ayacut are recorded with present available ayacut nil.

Every one of those orders records trade effluent NIL.

Across 11,583 granted water consents from the five Cooum-corridor TNPCB district offices (2021-2026), fifteen orders name the Cooum as a point of disposal, covering seven facilities, all municipal sewage plants. Nine industrial units near the river hold orders that expressly prohibit discharge of sewage or trade effluent to the Cooum.

methods.title: Length and chainage
methods.body: The 62.9 km alignment is chained from OpenStreetMap's river geometry (ODbL, snapshot August 2026): the Cooum is mapped as a single continuous way from the origin junction near Satharai to the mouth, resampled every 50 m. WRD's own DPR gives the river 65 km from the same origin; the difference is tracing generalisation. Whole-length uncertainty: about plus or minus 1-2%.

methods.title: Widths (the 1,258 transects)
methods.body: Every 50 m of chainage we cast a perpendicular line and measure the water-surface polygon traced by OpenStreetMap contributors (most edits 2021-2026). 1,049 transects return a measurement; the first seven kilometres have no mapped water surface (a rural, seasonal channel) and read unmeasured by design. 50 m sampling sits at the resolution of the source itself: the traced bank lines place a vertex every 22 m at the median, so sampling much finer would only re-read straight drawn edges. Width here is water surface at the tracing moment, not the river's recorded (poramboke) land. Each reach carries a confidence tier: A = at least 70% measured, tracing mostly 2021 or later, and width jitter at 200 m separation of 25% or less; B = measured but sparse or older tracing; C = not channel-measurable. Jitter is always evaluated at about 200 m separation, whatever the sampling density, so denser sampling cannot inflate a tier.

methods.title: Satellite metrics (Sentinel-2, 10 m pixels)
methods.body: Cloud-masked median composites: January-April and June-August 2026. Vegetation = NDVI above 0.35; open water = NDWI above 0. Vegetation on the water is computed strictly inside the mapped water polygons (floating plus emergent growth); corridor figures also include about 8 m of bank each side and read higher. The condition strip reads a 25 m disc every 50 m of chainage; with 10 m pixels, 50 m is the honest floor for this - finer bins would re-count the same pixels. Threshold choice moves fractions by roughly 5-10 percentage points; 10 m pixels undercount water in channels narrower than about 30 m. The suspended-sediment reading (NDTI) is a relative index over open water, not a mg/L measurement. Site images are clearest-pixel composites; segment images are medians; each is dated on the image.

methods.title: The built edge
methods.body: Google Open Buildings v3 footprints (2023 release, confidence at least 0.7) counted within 50 m and 100 m of the centerline. Deliberately conservative: measured from the centerline, not the river's recorded boundary; the confidence filter trims small structures; three years of construction post-date the data. A 'none mapped' reads exactly that: nothing in the dataset, not proof of nothing on the ground.

methods.title: Estimated widths (why this page ships none)
methods.body: The canal page fills its OSM-blind transects with labelled spectral estimates; this page deliberately does not. The Cooum's unmeasured stretch (the first seven kilometres) runs dry outside the diversion season - the estimator found water on only 9 of 203 blind transects - and its calibration against this river's OSM-measured transects failed our quality gate (water detected on 62 of 150; median disagreement 37.4 m, driven by weed-covered surfaces the near-infrared test reads as land). An estimate that calibrates this poorly would be a number without meaning, so the dots stay dots. The build applies this gate mechanically: estimates ship only where detection reaches half the measured transects and agreement is within 20 m.

methods.title: Check the numbers yourself
methods.body: Every input is public: OpenStreetMap (ODbL, snapshot date stated), Copernicus Sentinel-2, Google Open Buildings, and the cited government documents - many held as local primary copies (the WRD Cooum sub-basin DPR, the MAWS and WRD Policy Notes, NGT filings, TNPCB consent orders, CPCB monitoring PDFs, the CRZ clearance). Every derived number on this page is recomputed independently from the raw inputs before publication by a published audit script (scripts/audit_waterway_numbers_cooum.py in the Neer Vazhvu repository), and the claim register (claims.json) carries a per-number citation a reader can pull and compare.

methods.title: What this page deliberately does not compute
methods.body: Depth, silt volume and flow: no satellite can measure them in water this narrow and turbid, the river has no known public flow gauge, and we would rather show a gap than an estimate without an instrument. They are the first work of the measurement layer this page proposes: level and flow gauging, a boat-run depth survey, and field checks under the vegetation the satellite flags.
